Handoff-note read-back — does writing a short handover note pay for itself?
  format    references/orientation-and-threads.md §2b (the CSV and the read-back rules)
  pairing   a pair is a sitting with sessions in both arms; its value in an arm is the median of its sessions in that arm (the sitting is the block)
  rate      note_minutes converted at $100.00/hour = $1.6667/minute; change it with --minute-rate-usd. Every net-value number below moves with this rate, so it is stated here rather than buried in the code.

  session ends logged                3
  log lines skipped as malformed     0
  PENDING ends                       3   (a real sitting, no successor yet: not a data point)
  UNMATCHED ends                     0   (no sitting in the history has that folder)
  successor sessions joined          0   (—)
  usable pairs (sittings, both arms) 0

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNDERPOWERED: 0 usable pair(s), below the stated floor of 16.
Smallest effect this can detect, set in advance: 16 usable pairs detect "the note
wins in about 3 sittings out of 4" and nothing smaller. A real but modest effect
(the note helps 60 % of the time) will not show at that size. The honest report
of that result is "underpowered", not "no effect".
  (references/orientation-and-threads.md §2b, "What the read-back does")

for a successor; keep logging — the CSV is the artefact and the read-back is
retrospective.
